senses.sense_definition: To get off or climb down from a horse, bicycle, or other thing being ridden.

examples.text: Cyclists are required to <w>dismount</w> before crossing the busy pedestrian bridge.
The rider decided to <w>dismount</w> from the horse after finishing the long trail.

senses.sense_definition: To make a storage device or file system unavailable for use by the operating system.

examples.text: Always remember to <w>dismount</w> the drive before removing it from the computer.
The system could not <w>dismount</w> the external disk because another program was using it.

senses.sense_definition: To remove or knock a piece of heavy artillery, such as a cannon, off its carriage or mount.

examples.text: Heavy enemy fire managed to damage the rampart and <w>dismount</w> two large cannons.
Artillerymen worked through the night to repair and reposition the <w>dismounted</w> guns.

senses.sense_definition: To descend or come down from a higher place.

examples.text: In the poetic passage, the evening sun seemed to <w>dismount</w> slowly behind the western hills.
The birds began to <w>dismount</w> from the high branches as twilight approached.

senses.sense_definition: The act of detaching from an apparatus and landing on the floor at the end of a gymnastics routine.

examples.text: She executed a flawless routine but stumbled slightly on her final <w>dismount</w>.
The gymnast secured the gold medal with a clean and powerful <w>dismount</w>.

senses.sense_definition: The act of stepping down or getting off something being ridden.

examples.text: He made a smooth <w>dismount</w> from the bicycle when he reached the gate.
The skater landed a difficult trick and completed an impressive <w>dismount</w>.
